problem: Let $C={{c}_{1},{c}_{2}}$ be a basis of ${R}^{2}$ and $[x]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3\end{aligned}].$ What are the coordinates of $x$ relative to the basis $B={{b}_{1},{b}_{2}},$ where ${b}_{1}=\frac{1}{3}{c}_{2}$ and ${b}_{2}=2{c}_{1}?$

feedback.problem: Let $B={{b}_{1},{b}_{2}}$ be a basis of ${R}^{2}$ and $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -6\end{aligned}].$ What are the coordinates of $x$ relative to the basis $C={{c}_{1},{c}_{2}},$ where ${c}_{1}=5{b}_{2}$ and ${c}_{2}=-2{b}_{1}?$
feedback.worked_solution:
Since $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -6\end{aligned}]$, we can write $x$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =3{b}_{1}-6{b}_{2} \\  & =-6{b}_{2}+3{b}_{1} \\  & =-\frac{6}{5}(5{b}_{2})-\frac{3}{2}(-2{b}_{1}) \\  & =-\frac{6}{5}{c}_{1}-\frac{3}{2}{c}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $[x]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{6}{5} \\ -\frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}].$
